entry.title: Zcash Drops 21% From Recent High—Here’s Why the Rally May Not Be Over
entry.summary: ZEC is 21% off its $1,698 peak after ETF outflows and a suspected North Korean heist routed money through its shielded pool. Is the run over, or will traders buy the dip?

entry.title: SEC Proposes Rules to Clear Up How Advisers and Funds Can Hold Crypto
entry.summary: The proposal would let advisers and funds use state trust companies as custodians and permit self-custody under certain conditions, aiming to replace years of ambiguity with a clear compliance path.

entry.title: Reddit Is Killing RSS Feeds and Public API Access to Fight AI Scrapers
entry.summary: Reddit RSS dies November 13 and outside apps lose their data pipeline by March 2027. Reddit blames scraping bots, though it licenses its own content to AI companies.

entry.title: OpenAI Says People Linked to China's Moonshot Tried to Copy Its AI's Hidden Reasoning
entry.summary: OpenAI says it disrupted a campaign involving 15,000+ users and ties a core cluster to people associated with Moonshot, the startup behind Kimi.

entry.title: Meta Pushes Back on Claim That Muse AI Read a User's Messages Without Consent
entry.summary: Communications chief Andy Stone said reading Messages requires two permissions the user controls, disputing a journalist who reported Muse synced his texts despite his settings.

entry.title: The 'Largest Pure-Play' XRP Treasury Is About to Go Public
entry.summary: Shareholders approved Evernorth's merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II, clearing the way for the Ripple-backed firm to begin trading Oct. 8 with a stash of roughly 473 million XRP.

entry.title: OpenAI Fires Three Safety Researchers Over Alleged Leak to Outside Group
entry.summary: OpenAI says the three broke its rules on handling sensitive information. The exits land after months of rogue-agent incidents, a trail of safety-team departures, and a new lawsuit.

entry.title: It's the Start of Uptober. Will Bitcoin Live Up to It?
entry.summary: Bitcoin enters its historically strongest month after a record-pace September, but a Fed hike and 5.3% Treasury yields are testing the bulls.

entry.title: Illinois Delays Controversial Crypto Tax Amid Industry Lawsuit
entry.summary: Illinois officials and crypto groups jointly asked a state court to delay the 0.2% Digital Asset Tax from Jan. 1 to July 1, 2027, while a legal challenge continues.

entry.title: Near Intents Hacked for $3.8M Days After Denying North Korea-Linked Bitget Hacker
entry.summary: Near Intents froze its cross-chain swaps after a bug let an attacker drain about $3.8 million. The company promised to repay every user.

entry.title: Minecraft, Candy Crush Among 11 Games in EU Virtual Currency Crackdown
entry.summary: The guidelines exclude cryptocurrencies, leaving tokens outside a regime written for currencies bought with real money inside games.

entry.summary: Plus, a major MetaMask security event has crypto natives on edge as details trickle out.

entry.title: Citi Lifts 12-Month Bitcoin Target to $113K, Ethereum to $3K
entry.summary: The bank has revised its 12-month target for BTC up from $82K, though it remains about 10% below Bitcoin's October 2025 record.

entry.title: MetaMask Exits Lido Validators Amid Infrastructure ‘Security Incident’
entry.summary: The wallet says it has found no immediate threat to user wallets, but the ETH it is pulling out of Lido could take 45 days to return.

entry.summary: Regulators are probing how the exchange keeps serving EU customers from Abu Dhabi, months after it lost its MiCA registrations.

entry.title: Dogecoin Is Getting Apps as DogeOS Opens Its Public Testnet
entry.summary: The team behind the MyDoge wallet opened a public test of DogeOS, a layer that lets developers build lending platforms and games on top of the meme coin network.

entry.title: FBI Tells Its Employees to Assume Hackers Have Their Personal Data

entry.summary: The Coinbase-backed group's first Senate endorsements—Republicans Jon Husted and Ashley Hinson and Democrat Chris Pappas—come two weeks after the Clarity Act's collapse, as the industry's fight shifts to the campaign trail.
